def test_encode():
    # swapcase runs BEFORE vowel replacement â the trap in this function
    assert encode("hello") == "HGLLQ"      # HELLO -> E->G, O->Q
    assert encode("aeiou") == "CGKQW"      # swapcase -> AEIOU, then +2 each
    assert encode("AEIOU") == "cgkqw"      # swapcase -> aeiou, then +2 each
    assert encode("Hello World") == "hGLLQ wQRLD"
    assert encode("xyz") == "XYZ"          # no vowels: case swap only
    assert encode("") == ""
    assert encode("123!@#") == "123!@#"
```

Why these values: `vowels_replace` maps `aâc, eâg, iâk, oâq, uâw` (and uppercase equivalents), but `swapcase()` runs first, so the vowel you replace is the *swapped* one. Case is preserved through the replacement.
